name: Interactive 3D Website
philosophy: The product is an object you can handle. The site is a showroom built around one 3D subject, and interaction replaces description.
principles: One hero object, not a scene full of things
Touching it teaches something: each interaction reveals a real feature
The poster must already sell it before WebGL loads
Interface stays out of the way of the object
visualIdentity: A studio: clean stage, controlled lighting, generous negative space, interface labels that attach to the object like annotations.
artDirection: Direct the object like a product shoot: lighting, material, camera angles chosen per section. The page background is the studio backdrop.

layout.composition: The object anchors the composition and moves between sections, with text placed around it. Few, large sections.

typography: Precise and technical: clean display type with small annotation labels, numerals for specifications.
colour: Neutral stage colours that make the object's material the richest thing on the page.
contentPresentation: Short feature statements tied to parts of the object, then a specification list and a call to action.
assets: A licensed or authored glTF model under 3 MB with a poster for every scene. Procedural geometry is allowed when it is on purpose.
animation: Drag or orbit, camera moves tied to scroll, hotspots that focus the camera. Idle motion is subtle.
scrolling: Native scroll drives camera interpolation between saved views.
responsive: Mobile keeps the object with touch rotation or falls to the poster. Profile mobile: the team removed 3D for stutter on one site.
useCases: Data shown as a spatial object

compatibleWith.when: The story needs pinned chapters around the object; use APP-07 for a flagship

fromTeam: Workbook: real-time 3D with cursor and camera; scroll-driven camera, lazy GLB, HTML overlays synced to scroll; mobile unprofiled
